item.title: Albanian Premier Blames Oppsition for Stoking Anger and Protests
item.description: Albanian Prime Minister Edi Rama accused the opposition and unnamed “foreign forces” of stoking violent protests, saying the demonstrations were an attempt to derail the country’s efforts to join the European Union.
item.dc:creator: Gresa Kraja

item.title: Romania Says Russia Attacking Black Sea Route for Ukraine Ships
item.description: Russia is increasingly targeting Ukraine’s grain export corridors in the Black Sea and that increases security risks for the entire region, Romanian President Nicusor Dan said on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Andra Timu and Oliver Crook

item.title: The French Political Crisis Turning Into a Debt Crisis
item.description: Just about everyone is worried about what is going on in France right now: the country's public finances are in sorry shape and there are fears that the French bond selloff, and the country's growing debt crisis, might spillover into the rest of Europe. The 2027 elections have investors worried: Marine Le Pen and Jean-Luc Mélenchon aren't seen to be up to the task of taming France's fiscal turmoil. Shahin Vallée was an advisor to Emmanuel Macron when he was an economic minister and during his first presidential election campaign. He is currently a senior fellow at the German Council of Foreign Relations and advises institutional investors — and he understands what went wrong during Macron's nine years in office. Today, he speaks to us about the origins of the current French debt crisis, how similar it is to the challenges Greece faced during the first euro crisis, and why the 2027 elections are making an unstable situation even worse. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Latvian PM: Europe Is Zelenskyy’s Only Ally Now
item.description: Latvian Prime Minister Andris Kulbergs says “Zelenskyy has only one ally now, it’s actually the Europeans,” as US-Ukraine tensions continue. He made the comments in an exclusive live interview with BTV’s Oliver Crook on the second day of the European leaders summit in Brussels on Friday. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Europe Is Zelenskyy’s Only Ally Now, Latvian Leader Says
item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has only one ally now and that’s Europe, the Latvian prime minister said, referring to Kyiv’s spiraling tensions with the US.
item.dc:creator: Aaron Eglitis and Oliver Crook

item.title: Republican Sullivan Touts Trump Pushback in Alaska Senate Debate
item.description: Republican Senator Dan Sullivan emphasized where he differs from Donald Trump, just days after the president headlined an Alaska rally for his embattled reelection campaign.
item.dc:creator: Anna Edgerton

item.title: UK's Healey Plans to Raise Bank Taxes
item.description:
Bloomberg Daybreak Europe is your essential morning viewing to stay ahead. Live from Brussels, we set the agenda for your day, catching you up with overnight markets news from the US and Asia. And we'll tell you what matters for investors in Europe, giving you insight before trading begins.
On today's show, global stocks bounced back as dip buyers stepped in after the chip selloff.
The European Union is preparing to create new trade powers that could completely shut off access to its single market as part of a dramatic new push to cut the trade deficit with China.
And UK Chancellor of the Exchequer John Healey is set to raise taxes on banks to fund cost-of-living support for voters and stabilize the public finances, as he looks for sources of revenue that won’t violate Labour Party campaign pledges.
Today's guest: Suki Cooper, Standard Chartered, Global Head of Commodities Research. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Europe Prepares for World Where Trump Sides With Putin
item.description: US President Trump trashed years of energy sanctions on the Kremlin, pressured Kyiv to quit bombing Russian oil refineries and suggested Ukraine’s Volodymyr Zelenskyy was an illegitimate leader. Now, European Union leaders are preparing for a world where Trump effectively sides with Moscow as he menaces Ukraine and offers Russia an economic lifeline. EU leaders are meeting in Brussels and Zelenskyy will address the summit on Friday. Bloomberg's Oliver Crook reports. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Philippine President May Summon China Envoy for Veiled ‘Threat’
item.description: Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. may summon China’s ambassador, who appeared to suggest Beijing could easily win a conflict with the Philippines if it used force.
item.dc:creator: Cliff Venzon

item.title: Trump’s AI Task Force to Commission Report on Technology’s Risks
item.description: President Donald Trump’s artificial intelligence task force in its first meeting agreed on Thursday to address risks related to cybersecurity, biosecurity and “model control and accountability” as fears rise over the potential dangers posed by the technology.
item.dc:creator: John Harney

item.title: Why Starshield, US Military Satellites Are So Vital to Ukraine’s Defense
item.description: In the face of Russian missile and drone attacks, Ukraine needs more than weapons to protect itself. Satellites provide a crucial early warning that a projectile has been launched, as well as information on how to intercept it.
item.dc:creator: Gerry Doyle

item.title: Carney Rallies Remain Vote in Alberta as Crucial Referendum Nears
item.description: Prime Minister Mark Carney urged voters in Alberta to reject separatism in a referendum next week, saying it’s important for Canada to display unity and push back against those who want to see the country break apart.
item.dc:creator: Iain Boekhoff and Derek Decloet

item.title: Trump Muses on Future Iran Strike With ‘Mother of All Bombs’
item.description: President Donald Trump declined to rule out using a weapon known as the “Mother of all Bombs” on Iran after the US midterm elections.
item.dc:creator: Kate Sullivan

item.title: Portugal Housing Protest Ends as France Braces for Rallies
item.description: A housing protest in Portugal’s second-largest city was called off early Friday after organizers decided to disperse the gathering amid the presence of groups they identified as violent, following clashes with police earlier in the day.
item.dc:creator: Henrique Almeida

item.title: Singapore Probing Firms Over Haze-Causing Indonesian Fires
item.description: Singapore Prime Minister Lawrence Wong vowed to investigate firms responsible for fires that have shrouded the city-state in haze for weeks, warning those found culpable could face legal action.
item.dc:creator: Cindy Wang and Hallie Gu

item.title: Trump Seeks Culprits With Texas Senate Seat, Others in Peril
item.description: President Donald Trump railed at Senator John Cornyn of Texas and longtime GOP strategist Karl Rove, accusing them of undermining Ken Paxton’s Senate campaign in the state, a crucial contest for Republican hopes of retaining control of the chamber.
item.dc:creator: Kate Sullivan

item.title: Bolsonaro, Lula in Tight Race Ahead of Runoff, Poll Shows
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro and President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva are locked in a close race ahead of Brazil’s runoff election, according to a new poll.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Rosati and Augusta Saraiva

item.title: Ukraine Faces New World in Which Europe Is Its Only True Ally
item.description: European leaders know they can’t stop courting Donald Trump. But as the US president menaces Ukraine and offers Russia an economic lifeline, they are preparing for a world where he effectively sides with Moscow.
item.dc:creator: Andrea Palasciano, Alberto Nardelli and Ott Tammik

item.title: Trump Press Secretary Says She Didn’t Pass Bar, Downplays Result
item.description: White House Press Secretary Katie Zacharia acknowledged Thursday that she did not pass the California bar exam, but downplayed the results as she sought to get past mounting questions over her legal credentials.
item.dc:creator: Courtney Subramanian and Kate Sullivan

item.title: Zelenskyy Orders New Russia Refinery Attacks in Trump Rebuke
item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy ordered attacks on Russian oil refineries to resume in a spiraling confrontation with Donald Trump over restrictions on US intelligence assistance.
item.dc:creator: Aliaksandr Kudrytski and Daryna Krasnolutska
